primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Primary membranous nephropathy commonly features podocyte-directed autoimmunity and granular immune deposits on the epithelial side of the glomerular basement membrane, producing capillary-wall thickening and a spike-and-dome pattern.
vignette: A 52-year-old man has progressive edema and frothy urine. Laboratory studies show nephrotic-range proteinuria and hypoalbuminemia. Kidney biopsy shows diffuse capillary-wall thickening, granular IgG along glomerular capillary loops, and subepithelial electron-dense deposits.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?
distractor_notes: Minimal change disease has nearly normal light microscopy, negative immunofluorescence, and diffuse foot-process effacement.
IgA nephropathy shows mesangial IgA deposition and a nephritic phenotype.
Poststreptococcal GN is nephritic and typically has subepithelial humps rather than diffuse membranous capillary-wall deposits.
Diabetic nephropathy produces mesangial expansion and nodular sclerosis rather than granular subepithelial immune deposits.
key_expl: Adult nephrotic syndrome with diffuse capillary-wall thickening, granular IgG, and subepithelial deposits is classic for membranous nephropathy.
objective: Recognize membranous nephropathy from its nephrotic presentation and subepithelial immune-complex pattern.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Obstruction of hepatic venous outflow, usually by hepatic-vein thrombosis in a hypercoagulable state, causes sinusoidal congestion, painful hepatomegaly, ascites, and centrilobular hypoxic injury.
vignette: A 32-year-old woman taking an estrogen-containing oral contraceptive develops progressive right upper quadrant pain, abdominal distention, and tender hepatomegaly. Doppler ultrasonography shows absent flow in two hepatic veins and a patent portal vein.
distractor_notes: Portal vein thrombosis obstructs portal inflow rather than hepatic venous outflow and would not produce absent flow specifically in hepatic veins.
Constrictive pericarditis can cause hepatic congestion but is a cardiac cause and would not explain direct hepatic-vein thrombosis.
Acute viral hepatitis causes hepatocellular inflammation rather than hepatic venous outflow obstruction.
Primary biliary cholangitis is autoimmune small intrahepatic bile-duct destruction causing cholestasis, not hepatic-vein occlusion.
key_expl: Painful hepatomegaly and ascites in a hypercoagulable patient with Doppler evidence of hepatic-vein occlusion is Budd-Chiari syndrome.
objective: Recognize Budd-Chiari syndrome as hepatic venous outflow obstruction causing painful hepatomegaly and ascites.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Osteoid osteoma is a small benign bone-forming tumor with a vascular osteoid nidus and surrounding reactive sclerosis; high local prostaglandin production contributes to severe nocturnal pain that characteristically responds to NSAIDs.
vignette: A 17-year-old boy has several months of focal tibial pain that is worst at night and rapidly improves after ibuprofen. CT shows a small radiolucent cortical nidus surrounded by dense reactive sclerosis.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?
distractor_notes: Osteoblastoma is generally larger, often affects the posterior spine, and pain is less characteristically relieved by NSAIDs.
Osteosarcoma is an aggressive malignant osteoid-producing tumor with destructive metaphyseal features rather than a small cortical nidus.
Ewing sarcoma is a malignant small-round-cell tumor with destructive bone lesions and systemic features.
A Brodie abscess can mimic a lucent lesion with sclerosis but does not classically produce the highly characteristic nocturnal NSAID-responsive pain pattern.
key_expl: A young patient with focal nocturnal bone pain relieved by NSAIDs and a small radiolucent nidus with surrounding sclerosis has an osteoid osteoma.
objective: Recognize osteoid osteoma from its characteristic nocturnal NSAID-responsive pain and radiographic nidus.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Tissue-transglutaminase-mediated enhancement of gliadin immunogenicity in celiac disease
mechanism: Tissue transglutaminase 2 deamidates gliadin peptides, increasing their affinity for HLA-DQ2/DQ8 and thereby enhancing pathogenic CD4 T-cell activation in celiac disease.
vignette: A patient with chronic diarrhea, iron-deficiency anemia, and villous atrophy improves after eliminating gluten from the diet.
lead: Which biochemical modification of dietary gliadin most directly enhances its presentation to pathogenic T cells?
distractors: Gamma-carboxylation by a vitamin K-dependent enzyme
distractor_notes: Gamma-carboxylation is a vitamin K-dependent modification of specific proteins, not the key celiac mechanism.
Prolyl hydroxylation is important in collagen synthesis.
PKA-mediated phosphorylation does not create the immunogenic gliadin peptides central to celiac disease.
Histone acetylation is unrelated to luminal gliadin processing.
key_expl: tTG2 deamidates gliadin peptides, increasing their binding to HLA-DQ2/DQ8 and promoting a CD4 T-cell inflammatory response that damages small-intestinal villi.
objective: Explain how tissue transglutaminase increases gliadin immunogenicity in celiac disease.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Acid entering the duodenum stimulates S cells to release secretin. Secretin activates Gs-coupled receptors on pancreatic ductal/centroacinar cells, increasing cAMP and secretion of bicarbonate-rich fluid.
vignette: Acidic chyme enters the duodenum after a meal. Shortly afterward, pancreatic juice becomes markedly enriched in bicarbonate.
lead: Which hormone most directly mediates this response?
distractor_notes: CCK mainly stimulates pancreatic enzyme secretion and gallbladder contraction.
Gastrin promotes gastric acid secretion.
Motilin coordinates the fasting migrating motor complex.
Ghrelin promotes appetite and has no primary role in pancreatic bicarbonate secretion.
key_expl: Duodenal acid releases secretin from S cells. Secretin signals through cAMP to pancreatic ductal/centroacinar cells, increasing bicarbonate and water secretion that neutralize gastric acid.
objective: Identify secretin as the principal hormonal stimulus for bicarbonate-rich pancreatic secretion after acid enters the duodenum.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Cholecystokinin response to dietary fat and amino acids
mechanism: Fatty acids and amino acids in the duodenum/jejunum stimulate I cells to release CCK, which contracts the gallbladder, relaxes the sphincter of Oddi, and stimulates pancreatic enzyme secretion.
vignette: A meal rich in fat and protein enters the duodenum. The gallbladder contracts, the sphincter of Oddi relaxes, and pancreatic acinar enzyme secretion increases.
lead: Which gastrointestinal hormone is primarily responsible?
distractor_notes: Secretin primarily promotes bicarbonate-rich pancreatic and biliary fluid secretion in response to acid.
Somatostatin broadly inhibits gastrointestinal secretion and hormone release.
Motilin drives fasting migrating motor complexes.
Gastrin primarily stimulates gastric acid secretion and mucosal growth.
key_expl: CCK is released from intestinal I cells in response to fats and amino acids. Its coordinated effects include gallbladder contraction, sphincter of Oddi relaxation, and increased pancreatic digestive-enzyme secretion.
objective: Identify CCK as the hormone coordinating bile delivery and pancreatic enzyme secretion after a fat- and protein-rich meal.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: SGLT1-mediated intestinal glucose and galactose uptake
mechanism: Apical SGLT1 couples glucose or galactose uptake to the inward sodium gradient generated by basolateral Na+/K+ ATPase, making monosaccharide entry a secondary active transport process.
vignette: An enterocyte absorbs glucose from the intestinal lumen even when intracellular glucose concentration is higher than luminal concentration.
lead: Which process provides the immediate driving force for apical glucose uptake?
correct: Inward sodium electrochemical gradient maintained by basolateral Na+/K+ ATPase
distractors: Direct ATP hydrolysis by SGLT1 at the apical membrane
Outward chloride gradient generated by CFTR
Passive glucose diffusion through apical GLUT2 under fasting conditions
Proton gradient generated by a gastric H+/K+ ATPase
distractor_notes: SGLT1 does not directly hydrolyze ATP; it uses the sodium gradient.
CFTR chloride movement is not the driver of SGLT1 glucose uptake.
Brush-border glucose/galactose uptake is primarily via SGLT1 in this construct, not passive apical GLUT2 diffusion.
Gastric H+/K+ ATPase is unrelated to enterocyte SGLT1 energetics.
key_expl: Basolateral Na+/K+ ATPase keeps intracellular sodium low. SGLT1 exploits this sodium gradient to cotransport sodium with glucose or galactose across the apical membrane against the monosaccharide concentration gradient.
objective: Explain intestinal glucose/galactose uptake as secondary active transport driven by the sodium gradient created by Na+/K+ ATPase.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Electrical coupling of cardiomyocytes through gap junctions
mechanism: Connexin-based gap junctions in intercalated discs form low-resistance channels that permit direct ion flow between adjacent cardiomyocytes, enabling rapid cell-to-cell propagation of depolarization.
vignette: A myocardial biopsy shows intact contractile filaments but selective disruption of the intercellular channels that allow ions to pass directly from one cardiomyocyte to the next.
lead: Which cardiac function would be most directly impaired?
correct: Rapid electrical propagation between adjacent cardiomyocytes
distractors: Attachment of actin filaments to the extracellular basement membrane
Anchoring of intermediate filaments between cardiomyocytes only
Calcium storage within the sarcoplasmic reticulum
ATP production by mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation
distractor_notes: Cell-matrix attachment is mediated by other adhesion systems, not gap junctions.
Desmosomes provide mechanical intermediate-filament linkage; the described ion channels are gap junctions.
Sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium storage is intracellular and independent of gap-junction channels.
Mitochondrial ATP production is not the direct function of intercalated-disc gap junctions.
key_expl: Gap junctions within intercalated discs allow ions to move directly between neighboring cardiomyocytes, electrically coupling the cells so depolarization spreads rapidly and contraction is coordinated.
objective: Relate cardiac gap junctions to low-resistance intercellular electrical coupling and synchronized myocardial activation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Loss of E-cadherin-mediated adhesion in invasive lobular breast carcinoma
mechanism: CDH1 inactivation causes loss of E-cadherin, reducing epithelial cell-cell adhesion and producing the characteristic discohesive single-file infiltration pattern of invasive lobular carcinoma.
vignette: A breast biopsy shows small malignant cells infiltrating the stroma in single-file cords. Immunohistochemistry is negative for E-cadherin.
lead: Loss of which cellular function most directly explains this morphology?
distractors: Cadherin-independent anchoring of keratin to hemidesmosomes
distractor_notes: Integrins mediate cell-matrix adhesion, not the E-cadherin-dependent cell-cell cohesion lost in lobular carcinoma.
Connexins form gap junctions and do not account for single-file discohesion.
Mitotic spindle function is not the direct consequence of E-cadherin loss.
Hemidesmosomes are cell-matrix junctions and use integrins rather than E-cadherin.
key_expl: E-cadherin is a calcium-dependent cell-cell adhesion molecule encoded by CDH1. Its loss causes cells to become discohesive, producing the classic single-file growth pattern of invasive lobular carcinoma.
objective: Connect E-cadherin loss in invasive lobular carcinoma to defective epithelial cell-cell adhesion.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: HLA-DM-mediated removal of CLIP from MHC class II
mechanism: MHC class II molecules leave the ER associated with invariant chain. After invariant-chain degradation in endosomal compartments, CLIP remains in the peptide-binding groove until HLA-DM facilitates CLIP removal and loading of exogenous antigenic peptides.
vignette: An antigen-presenting cell internalizes a bacterial protein and degrades it in an acidified endosomal compartment. MHC class II molecules arrive in the same compartment with CLIP occupying their peptide-binding grooves.
lead: Which molecule most directly facilitates removal of CLIP so the bacterial peptide can bind?
distractor_notes: TAP1 transports cytosolic peptides into the ER for MHC class I loading.
Beta2-microglobulin is a structural component of MHC class I.
Tapasin assists peptide loading onto MHC class I molecules.
Calnexin is an ER chaperone involved in MHC class I assembly and other protein folding.
key_expl: HLA-DM acts in MHC class II loading compartments to promote release of CLIP from the peptide-binding groove and facilitate binding/editing of endosomally derived antigenic peptides for presentation to CD4 T cells.
objective: Identify HLA-DM as the facilitator of CLIP removal and exogenous peptide loading onto MHC class II.
